biothings.name: panic disorder without agoraphobia
biothings.definition: A disorder in which an individual experiences recurrent, unexpected panic attacks and persistent concern about having additional panic attacks. Agoraphobia is not a component of this disorder. [NCIT:C97193]

biothings.name: panic disorder with agoraphobia
biothings.definition: A disorder in which an individual experiences recurrent, unexpected panic attacks and persistent concern about having additional panic attacks. Agoraphobia is a component of this disorder. [NCIT:C97194]

biothings.name: agoraphobia
biothings.definition: An anxiety disorder characterized by an intense, irrational fear of venturing out into open places or situations in which help (or escape) might not be available should excessive anxiety or panic symptoms develop. [NCIT:P378]

opentargets.name: agoraphobia
opentargets.description: An anxiety disorder characterized by an intense, irrational fear of venturing out into open places or situations in which help (or escape) might not be available should excessive anxiety or panic symptoms develop.

opentargets.name: panic disorder without agoraphobia
opentargets.description: A disorder in which an individual experiences recurrent, unexpected panic attacks and persistent concern about having additional panic attacks. Agoraphobia is not a component of this disorder.

opentargets.name: panic disorder
opentargets.description: An anxiety disorder characterized by multiple unexpected panic attacks with persistent concern of recurring attacks. Panic disorder may or may not be accompanied by agoraphobia.

opentargets.name: stiff-person syndrome
opentargets.description: Stiff-man syndrome (SMS) is a rare neurological disorder comprising fluctuating trunk and limb stiffness, painful muscle spasms, task-specific phobia, an exaggerated startle response, and ankylosing deformities such as fixed lumbar hyperlordosis.

opentargets.name: agoraphobia symptom measurement
opentargets.description: quantification of some aspect of agoraphobia symptoms such as their frequency or severity, usually via a structured questionnaire such as the Agoraphobia Cognition Questionnaire (ACQ)
